applyTo: "_pages/**/*.md,_projects/**/*.md,_data/cv.yml,_data/software.yml,_data/research_figures.yml,assets/img/research/**/*"

# Academic content

Write for researchers, public-health colleagues, students and readers outside the
specialty. Introduce the scientific question and purpose before package internals.
Use direct sentences, descriptive headings and meaningful link text. Expand an
acronym on its first substantive use on each standalone page. Retain technical
terms when they clarify the claim; explain them in ordinary language first.

Describe current work with verbs such as "study", "develop" and "assess". Separate
implemented capabilities, research aims and published findings. State release
availability and development stage accurately. Link public papers and artifacts;
keep private methods, results, data and submission plans out of public content.
A target venue is not evidence of acceptance.

Use the introduction to describe the research questions, methods and scientific
applications. Reserve "partially observed" for a specific latent-state or
measurement model and explain what is observed. Use "structured" with the
relevant organization, such as age, space or traits. Use "complex systems" when
interactions and collective behavior are the subject. These terms describe
different features; avoid substituting them for one another or using them as
generic research labels.

Use terminology that matches the evidence:

- Describe constraint satisfaction or compliance directly. Reserve "metric" for
  objects with the required mathematical properties and "proper scoring rule" for
  its statistical meaning.
- A constraint check on a computed example describes that example and domain.
  Satisfaction by construction requires a separate justification. Neither alone
  establishes predictive accuracy or scientific adequacy.
- An evaluation made before an outcome is observed may use information available
  when the prediction is issued. Avoid implying that it uses no observations.
- Describe a predictive ensemble as calibrated only for an assessed calibration
  property. Simulation-based calibration assesses inference under the assumed
  generative model; observed-data adequacy needs separate evaluation.
- Identification and recovery depend on the model, observation process and stated
  assumptions. Arbitrary-point evaluation does not establish grid convergence.
- Software stage labels describe development maturity, not scientific validity.
  OP System and OP Engine include spatial, nonlocal, compartmental and stochastic
  models. An ODE example represents one supported use.

Captions and text alternatives should state what a figure actually shows. Label
constructed illustrations and synthetic computations. Keep numerical accuracy,
spatial convergence, uncertainty calibration and application evidence distinct.
Choose a diagram structure from its content; use numbered steps for an actual
ordered procedure. Avoid slogans, unsupported novelty or performance claims,
repeated caveats, and punctuation used in place of sentence structure.

These are editorial rules, not a claim of accessibility conformance. Related
public guidance:

- [Berkeley on personal academic webpages](https://townsendcenter.berkeley.edu/blog/personal-academic-webpages-how-tos-and-tips-better-site)
- [W3C WAI on writing for web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tips/writing/)
- [W3C WAI on complex images](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/complex/)
